differences.title: 1. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Leverages PostgreSQL's robust relational model, offering strong typing, SQL queries, and ACID compliance for complex data structures.
differences.rightDesc: Uses a JSON-like key-value structure, optimized for fast reads and writes, suitable for simpler data models and rapid synchronization.

differences.title: 2. SYNC MECHANISM
differences.leftDesc: Tracks changes in Postgres using triggers/replication, pushing deltas to clients and receiving mutations for atomic commits.
differences.rightDesc: Employs Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs) or diffing strategies to merge concurrent client changes deterministically.

differences.title: 3. OFFLINE SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: Provides a fully functional, offline-first relational database on the client that syncs automatically when connectivity returns.
differences.rightDesc: Manages client-side state that synchronizes with the server, with explicit conflict resolution logic for offline operations.

differences.title: 4. SCHEMA MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Relies on the existing PostgreSQL schema and migrations. Schema changes are managed server-side and pushed down.
differences.rightDesc: Schema is defined within the client application logic and synchronized; server acts more as a transport/persister.

differences.title: 5. REAL-TIME UPDATES
differences.leftDesc: Utilizes PostgreSQL's LISTEN/NOTIFY or logical replication to efficiently push server-side changes to connected clients.
differences.rightDesc: Typically uses persistent WebSocket connections or RPC for immediate client-to-server and server-to-client communication.

differences.title: 6. SCALABILITY FOCUS
differences.leftDesc: Scales by leveraging PostgreSQL's mature scaling capabilities. Client data is a subset of server state.
differences.rightDesc: Optimized for many clients syncing concurrently. Server is a state management and sync coordination service.

differences.title: 7. DEVELOPMENT COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Requires familiarity with PostgreSQL, SQL, and database migrations. Sync logic is often managed by the tool.
differences.rightDesc: Focuses on client-side state management and conflict resolution. Server-side is simpler, often acting as a blob store.
